build.cpuBackend: interpreter (DBP's C_DYNAMIC_X86/C_DYNREC dynarecs are gated on host-CPU macros Emscripten never defines, so the core falls back to its own interpreter with no build-time flag needed)
notes: Built from the EmulatorJS fork of dosbox-pure (the only fork with a working platform=emscripten Makefile block), following the puae/play/mupen64plus_next recipe (docs/AMIGA_CORE_BUILD.md, scripts/cores/dos/build.sh).

First link attempt failed with undefined glMapBufferRange/glUnmapBuffer: the shared ~/amiga-build/RetroArch obj tree had gl2.o compiled with HAVE_OPENGLES3 from a prior core (N64/PS2), while this core's link line omitted it, so Makefile.emscripten took the FULL_ES2 LDFLAGS branch and disagreed with its own objects. Fixed by passing HAVE_OPENGLES3=1, same as N64/PS2 already document.

HAVE_THREADS=1 (unlike PUAE's HAVE_THREADS=0): DBP_ThreadControl spawns a genuine pthread_create()+semaphores pair, not the libco-fiber-via-Asyncify hack N64 needed. Untested at build time whether pthread_create() from inside this app's own dedicated execution Worker (a worker-in-worker topology no other core here has exercised) actually spawns and runs correctly in a browser — see the headless boot probe (scripts/probe-dos-core.js) for the real answer.
library_name confirmed as 'DOSBox-pure' by reading dosbox_pure_libretro.cpp:2073 directly, not guessed.

supported_extensions (from the core's own .info file) = zip|dosz|exe|com|bat|iso|chd|cue|ins|img|ima|vhd|jrc|m3u|m3u8|conf|/ ; needs_fullpath=true; supports_no_game=true (the core can boot to its own internal DOS shell with a trivial/empty .conf and no mounted disk at all).
